name: Question 15
worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =169 \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(169) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{2})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({y}^{2}) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2})+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2}) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (2x)+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot (2y) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, substituting the given information $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=5$ and $y=12,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (2x)+5\cdot (2(12)) & =0 \\ 2x\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+120 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

We also want to substitute for $x,$ but we are not given this value. However, we can find it by substituting $y=12$ into the equation of the circle.  

At the point where $y=12,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =169 \\ {x}^{2}+{12}^{2} & =169 \\ {x}^{2}+144 & =169 \\ {x}^{2} & =25 \\ x & =\pm 5.\end{aligned}
$$

We choose $x=5$ since we're only interested in the first quadrant. 

Finally, substituting $x=5,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}2x\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+120 & =0 \\ 2(5)\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+120 & =0 \\ 10\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =-120 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{-120}{10} \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =-12.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Differentiating the given relation with respect to t using implicit differentiation, we get

x2+y2=169ddt(x2+y2)=ddt(169)ddt(x2)+ddt(y2)=0dxdt⋅ddx(x2)+dydt⋅ddy(y2)=0dxdt⋅(2x)+dydt⋅(2y)=0.

Now, substituting the given information dydt=5 and y=12, we get dxdt⋅(2x)+5⋅(2(12))=02x⋅dxdt+120=0.

We also want to substitute for x, but we are not given this value. However, we can find it by substituting y=12 into the equation of the circle.

At the point where y=12, we have x2+y2=169x2+122=169x2+144=169x2=25x=±5.

We choose x=5 since we're only interested in the first quadrant.

Finally, substituting x=5, we get

2x⋅dxdt+120=02(5)⋅dxdt+120=010⋅dxdt=−120dxdt=−12010dxdt=−12.
